Secrecy in Special Branch

The Officers in charge of Sections of the Special
Branch should exercise the greatest care in guarding
secrets entrusted to their keeping, and it is incumbent
on all members of the staff to assist their seniors in
the discharge of this duty by being at pains to prevent
any leakage of information about inquiries on which they
are engaged themselves and by reporting without delay
any circumstance pointing to the possibility of the
existence of a leakage in any division of the office to
which they are attached. While laying down the following
rules for general guidance, the D.C. (Special Branch)
feels that the safeguarding of the secrets of the work
of the Branch must finally depend upon the loyalty,
carefulness and initiative of the staff, and a realization
on the part of every member of the Branch that there is
nothing so damaging to the reputation of a body engaged
on secret duties as leakages of information about the work
which is being done. While the exchange and discussion of
information is valuable, care must be taken not to let
this deteriorate into gossip.

The following rules are set down for general
guidance :-

1. With the exception of reports on routine matters and
ordinary labour or political affairs, all documents
of a confidential nature should as a rule be typed
by the officer in charge of the inquiries.

2. The initials of the person by whom it was typed
should be given at the top of each report.

3. Reports when typed should be handed personally by
the detective responsible for the inquiry to the
Officer in Charge of his Section.

特科的保密工作

特科各科主管警官在保管 entrusted 给他们的秘密时应格外小心，全体职员均有责任协助上级履行这一职责，务必防止泄露其自身所从事调查的任何信息，并立即报告任何表明其所属部门可能存在泄密情况的事由。在制定以下一般指导规则时，特科副总监认为，保护本科工作秘密最终必须依赖于职员的忠诚、谨慎和主动性，以及本科每位成员都认识到，对于从事秘密工作的机构而言，没有什么比泄露正在进行的工作信息更损害其声誉的了。虽然信息的交流和讨论很有价值，但必须注意不要使其沦为闲言碎语。

制定以下规则作为一般指导：-

1. 除关于日常事务和普通劳工或政治事务的报告外，所有机密性质的文件原则上应由负责调查的警官打字。

2. 每份报告的顶部应注明打字人的姓名首字母。

3. 报告打印好后，应由负责该调查的警探亲自交给其所在科的主管警官。

Special Branch
February 22, 1938.
（批：REGISTRY D. 2381 23 -2 38）

Secrecy in Special Branch

The Officers in charge of Sections of the Special
Branch should exercise the greatest care in guarding
secrets entrusted to their keeping, and it is incumbent
on all members of the staff to assist their seniors in
the discharge of this duty by being at pains to prevent
any leakage of information about inquiries on which they
are engaged themselves and by reporting without delay
any circumstance pointing to the possibility of the
existence of a leakage in any division of the office to
which they are attached. While laying down the following
rules for general guidance, the D.C. (Special Branch)
feels that the safeguarding of the secrets of the work
of the Branch must finally depend upon the loyalty,
carefulness and initiative of the staff, and a realization
on the part of every member of the Branch that there is
nothing so damaging to the reputation of a body engaged
on secret duties as leakages of information about the work
which is being done. While the exchange and discussion of
information is valuable, care must be taken not to let
this deteriorate into gossip.

The following rules are set down for general
guidance :-

1. With the exception of reports on routine matters and
ordinary labour or political affairs, all documents
of a confidential nature should as a rule be typed
by the officer in charge of the inquiries.
2. The initials of the person by whom it was typed
should be given at the top of each report.
3. Reports when typed should be handed personally by
the detective responsible for the inquiry to the
Officer in Charge of his Section.

特科的保密工作

特科各科主管警官在保管 entrusted 给他们的秘密时应格外小心，全体职员均有责任协助上级履行这一职责，务必防止泄露其自身所从事调查的任何信息，并立即报告任何表明其所属部门可能存在泄密情况的事由。在制定以下一般指导规则时，特科副总监认为，保护本科工作秘密最终必须依赖于职员的忠诚、谨慎和主动性，以及本科每位成员都认识到，对于从事秘密工作的机构而言，没有什么比泄露正在进行的工作信息更损害其声誉的了。虽然信息的交流和讨论很有价值，但必须注意不要使其沦为闲言碎语。

制定以下规则作为一般指导：-

1. 除关于日常事务和普通劳工或政治事务的报告外，所有机密性质的文件原则上应由负责调查的警官打字。
2. 每份报告的顶部应注明打字人的姓名首字母。
3. 报告打印好后，应由负责该调查的警探亲自交给其所在科的主管警官。

Special Branch, S.M.P.
June 21, 1935.

Secrecy in Special Branch.

The Officers in charge of Sections of the Special
Branch should exercise the greatest care in guarding
secrets entrusted to their keeping, and it is incumbent
on all members of the staff to assist their seniors in
the discharge of this duty by being at pains to prevent
any leakage of information about inquiries on which they
are engaged themselves and by reporting without delay
any circumstance pointing to the possibility of the
existence of a leakage in any division of the office to
which they are attached. While laying down the
following rules for general guidance, the D. C. (Sp.Br.)
feels that the safeguarding of the secrets of the work
of the Branch must finally depend upon the loyalty,
carefulness and initiative of the staff, and a realiza-
tion on the part of every member of the Branch that there
is nothing so damaging to the reputation of a body engaged
on secret duties as leakages of information about the
work which is being done.

The following rules are set down for general
guidance :-

1. With the exception of reports on routine matters
and ordinary labour or political affairs, all documents
should as a rule be typed by the officer in charge of
the inquiries.

2. The initials of the person by whom it was typed
should be given at the top of each report.

3. Reports when typed should be handed personally by the
detective responsible for the inquiry to the Officer
in Charge of his Section.

上海公共租界工部局警务处特别支部。
1935年6月21日。

特别支部的保密工作。

特别支部各股负责人在守护托付给他们的秘密时应极其谨慎，全体职员均有责任协助上级履行这一职责，务必防止泄露其自身所从事调查的任何信息，并立即报告任何表明其所属部门可能存在泄密情况的事态。在制定以下一般指导规则时，特别支部副总监认为，保护支部工作的秘密最终必须依赖于职员的忠诚、谨慎和主动性，以及支部每位成员都认识到，对于从事秘密工作的机构而言，没有什么比泄露正在进行的工作信息更损害其声誉的了。

制定以下规则以供一般指导：-

1. 除关于日常事务和普通劳工或政治事件的报告外，所有文件原则上应由负责调查的警官打字。

2. 每份报告的顶部应注明打字人的姓名首字母。

3. 报告打字完成后，应由负责该调查的侦探亲自交给其所在股的负责人。

pages.en:
- 2 -

4. On receiving a report the Officer in Charge of the
Section should see that they are stamped "Secret"
and passed without undue delay either personally or
in a locked or sealed container to the Officer in
Charge of the Registry.

5. The Officer in Charge of the Registry will handle all
confidential files passing to and from the D. C.(Sp.Br.)
and will attend personally to the indexing and filing
of these reports in the cabinet provided.

6. The Officer in Charge of the Registry should arrange
as soon as circumstances permit after the receipt of
confidential reports to show them to the P. A. to
D. C. (Sp.Br.) so that the latter will be acquainted
with all work undertaken in the Branch.

7. Copies of reports made by S. 2 should be retained
and kept effectively locked up by the Officer in Charge.
Not more than one spare copy of a report should be
retained by any Section, and special measures should be
taken in every case to ensure that these copies are
only seen by members of the staff who actually require
them in connection with their work.

8. Confidential files will only be obtainable from the
Registry upon production of an application form signed
by an Officer in Charge of a Section. Before handing
out a file of a specially secret nature or otherwise
of extraordinary importance, the Officer in Charge
of the Registry should refer the matter to the P. A.
or the D. C. (Sp.Br.) Applications for files should
be submitted in sealed covers and handed into the
Registry through the clerk at the Inquiry Desk. The
files should be sent to the officers by whom they are
required either personally by a responsible member of
the staff of the Registry or in a sealed cover.
pages.zh:
- 2 -

4. 股负责人收到报告后，应确保报告盖上“秘密”印章，并无不当延误地亲自或通过上锁或密封的容器，将其转交档案室负责人。

5. 档案室负责人将处理所有往来于特别支部副总监处的机密档案，并亲自负责将这些报告索引并存入指定的柜中。

6. 档案室负责人应在收到机密报告后，视情况尽快安排向特别支部副总监助理展示这些报告，以便后者了解支部开展的所有工作。

7. S. 2 制作的报告副本应由负责人保留并有效上锁保管。任何一股保留的报告备用副本不得超过一份，且在每种情况下都应采取特别措施，确保这些副本仅由工作中实际需要的职员查看。

8. 只有凭股负责人签名的申请表，方可从档案室获取机密档案。在分发具有特别秘密性质或其他异常重要性的档案之前，档案室负责人应将此事呈报助理或特别支部副总监。档案申请应以密封信封提交，并通过问询处文员递交至档案室。档案应由档案室的一名负责任职员亲自送达，或以密封信封方式，送交所需警官。

pages.en:
- 3 -

9. Applications for files received during the previous
twenty four hours should be submitted to the D.C.
(Sp.Br.) every morning at 10 a.m.

10. Notes and drafts of reports on confidential matters
should be destroyed by fire. Carbon paper used in
the typing of such reports should be locked up when
not in use. Drafts of reports should be made in
pencil so as to eliminate the possibility of leakages
of information through blotting paper.

11. Detectives' diaries and other papers containing notes
on cases should at all times be kept locked up. In
special cases detectives should be instructed not
to give details in their diaries of addresses visited
or names of persons about whom information is sought.
A blank space could be left and filled up after the
necessity for secrecy elapses.

12. The transmitting of messages of a secret nature by
telephone . should as far as possible be avoided.

13. All chit books and letters brought to headquarters by
messengers and others should in the first instance
be handed to the clerk at the Inquiry Desk who will
take them to the Officer in the Registry appointed to
receive and acknowledge such communications. He will
return the chit books or receipts to the messengers
after they have been duly signed.

14. All persons wishing to see the D. C. (Sp.Br.) or any
person working in Room 614, occupied by the Registry,
should present themselves at the Inquiry Desk and
arrange to see the person they are seeking by filling
up a slip on which they will state their own name,
the name of the person they wish to see and the nature
of their business. If the person sought happens to be
out, the slip should be taken to an appropriate
substitute.
pages.zh:
- 3 -

9. 每天上午10时，应将前二十四小时内收到的档案申请呈报特别支部副总监。

10. 关于机密事项的笔记和报告草稿应予以焚毁。用于打印此类报告的复写纸在不使用时应上锁保管。报告草稿应用铅笔书写，以消除通过吸墨纸泄露信息的可能性。

11. 侦探日记和其他包含案件笔记的文件应随时上锁保管。在特殊情况下，应指示侦探不在日记中记录所访问的地址或 sought 信息的人员姓名。可留出空白，待保密必要性消失后再填写。

12. 应尽可能避免通过电话传递秘密性质的信息。

13. 信差及其他人员带到总部的所有便条簿和信件，首先应交给问询处文员，由其转交给档案室指定的负责接收和确认此类通信的警官。在 duly 签署后，他将把便条簿或收据归还给信差。

14. 所有希望会见特别支部副总监或在档案室占用的614房间工作的任何人员的人，应前往问询处，并通过填写一张纸条来安排会见，纸条上需注明其本人姓名、希望会见者的姓名以及事由。如果被寻找的人恰好外出，该纸条应交给适当的代理人员。

pages.en:
- 4 -

15. Nobody is to be allowed to loiter in any Section and
nobody, apart from Officers in Charge of Sections,
should enter the Registry. Members of the public
should on no account be allowed to enter the
Registry unless brought there by the D. C. (Sp.Br.)
or an officer acting for him.
16. All communications with other branches of the Force
should be sent in special locked boxes.
17. Weekly Returns of Reports should not state the
subject to which they refer.
18. When files of an exceptionally confidential nature
or of great urgency have to be dealt with, the
D. C. (Sp. Br.) may depart from these rules and
make special arrangements in regard to the procedure
to be followed.

W Givens
Deputy Commissioner
(Special Branch)

Notes
by the
J.J. Jones
Mfan
pages.zh:
- 4 -

15. 任何人不得在任何股内逗留，除各股主管外，任何人不得进入档案室。公众成员除非由特别处副主任（D. C. (Sp.Br.)）或代表其行事的警官带领，否则绝不允许进入档案室。
16. 与本局其他部门的所有通信均应通过特制的上锁信箱发送。
17. 每周报告汇总不得注明其所涉主题。
18. 当需要处理性质特别机密或极为紧急的案卷时，特别处副主任（D. C. (Sp. Br.)）可偏离上述规则，并就应遵循的程序作出特别安排。

副局长

Branch should exercise the greatest care in guarding

in Charge of his Section.

Special Branch, S.M.P.
June 21, 1935.

Secrecy in Special Branch.

The Officers in charge of Sections of the Special
Branch should exercise the greatest care in guarding
secrets entrusted to their keeping, and it is incumbent
on all members of the staff to assist their seniors in
the discharge of this duty by being at pains to prevent
any leakage of information about inquiries on which they
are engaged themselves and by reporting without delay
any circumstance pointing to the possibility of the
existence of a leakage in any division of the office to
which they are attached. While laying down the
following rules for general guidance, the D. C. (Sp.Br.)
feels that the safeguarding of the secrets of the work
of the Branch must finally depend upon the loyalty,
carefulness and initiative of the staff, and a realiza-
tion on the part of every member of the Branch that there
is nothing so damaging to the reputation of a body engaged
on secret duties as leakages of information about the
work which is being done.

The following rules are set down for general
guidance :-

1. With the exception of reports on routine matters
and ordinary labour or political affairs, all documents
should as a rule be typed by the officer in charge of
the inquiries.

2. The initials of the person by whom it was typed
should be given at the top of each report.

3. Reports when typed should be handed personally by the
detective responsible for the inquiry to the Officer
in Charge of his Section.

1935年6月21日。

特务科的保密工作。

特务科各股主管官员在保管 entrusted 给他们的机密时应极其谨慎，全体职员均有责任协助上级履行此职责，务必防止泄露其自身所从事调查的任何信息，并立即报告任何表明其所属部门可能存在泄密情况的事态。在制定以下一般性指导规则时，特务科副总监（D. C. (Sp.Br.)）认为，保护本科工作机密的最终保障必须依赖于职员的忠诚、细心和主动性，以及本科每位成员都认识到，对于从事秘密工作的机构而言，没有什么比泄露正在进行的工作信息更损害其声誉的了。

1. 除关于例行事务及普通劳工或政治事件的报告外，所有文件原则上应由负责调查的官员打字。

2. 每份报告的顶部应注明打字人的姓名首字母。

3. 报告打印好后，应由负责该调查的警探亲自交给其所在股的主管官员。

Section should see that they are stamped "Secret"
and passed without undue delay either personally or
in a locked or sealed container to the Officer in
Charge of the Registry.

5. The Officer in Charge of the Registry will handle all
confidential files passing to and from the D. C.(Sp.Br.)
and will attend personally to the indexing and filing
of these reports in the cabinet provided.

6. The Officer in Charge of the Registry should arrange
as soon as circumstances permit after the receipt of
confidential reports to show them to the P. A. to
D. C. (Sp.Br.) so that the latter will be acquainted
with all work undertaken in the Branch.

7. Copies of reports made by S. 2 should be retained
and kept effectively locked up by the Officer in Charge.
Not more than one spare copy of a report should be
retained by any Section, and special measures should be
taken in every case to ensure that these copies are
only seen by members of the staff who actually require
them in connection with their work.

8. Confidential files will only be obtainable from the
Registry upon production of an application form signed
by an Officer in Charge of a Section. Before handing
out a file of a specially secret nature or otherwise
of extraordinary importance, the Officer in Charge
of the Registry should refer the matter to the P. A.
or the D. C. (Sp.Br.) Applications for files should
be submitted in sealed covers and handed into the
Registry through the clerk at the Inquiry Desk. The
files should be sent to the officers by whom they are
required either personally by a responsible member of
the staff of the Registry or in a sealed cover.

6. 档案室主管官员应在收到机密报告后，一旦情况允许，即安排向特务科副总监助理（P. A. to D. C. (Sp.Br.)）展示这些报告，以便后者了解本科承担的所有工作。

twenty four hours should be submitted to the D.C.
(Sp.Br.) every morning at 10 a.m.

should be destroyed by fire. Carbon paper used in
the typing of such reports should be locked up when
not in use. Drafts of reports should be made in
pencil so as to eliminate the possibility of leakages
of information through blotting paper.

11. Detectives' diaries and other papers containing notes
on cases should at all times be kept locked up. In
special cases detectives should be instructed not
to give details in their diaries of addresses visited
or names of persons about whom information is sought.
A blank space could be left and filled up after the
necessity for secrecy elapses.

12. The transmitting of messages of a secret nature by
telephone . should as far as possible be avoided.

13. All chit books and letters brought to headquarters by
messengers and others should in the first instance
be handed to the clerk at the Inquiry Desk who will
take them to the Officer in the Registry appointed to
receive and acknowledge such communications. He will
return the chit books or receipts to the messengers
after they have been duly signed.

person working in Room 614,occupied by the Registry,
should present themselves at the Inquiry Desk and
arrange to see the person they are seeking by filling
up a slip on which they will state their own name,
the name of the person they wish to see and the nature
of their business. If the person sought happens to be
out, the slip should be taken to an appropriate
substitute.

nobody, apart from Officers in Charge of Sections,
should enter the Registry. Members of the public
should on · no account be allowed to enter the
Registry unless brought there by the D. C. (Sp.Br.)
or an officer acting for him.
16. All communications with other branches of the Force
should be sent in special locked boxes.
17. Weekly Returns of Reports should not state the
subject to which they refer.
18. When files of an exceptionally confidential nature
or of great urgency have to be dealt with, the
D. C. (Sp. Br.) may depart from these rules and
make special arrangements in regard to the procedure
to be followed.

Deputy Commissioner
(Special Branch)

Special Branch, S.M.P.
June 21, 1935.

Secrecy in Special Branch.

The Officers in charge of Sections of the Special
Branch should exercise the greatest care in guarding
secrets entrusted to their keeping, and it is incumbent
on all members of the staff to assist their seniors in
the discharge of this duty by being at pains to prevent
any leakage of information about inquiries on which they
are engaged themselves and by reporting without delay
any circumstance pointing to the possibility of the
existence of a leakage in any division of the office to
which they are attached. While laying down the
following rules for general guidance, the D. C. (Sp.Br.)
feels that the safeguarding of the secrets of the work
of the Branch must finally depend upon the loyalty,
carefulness and initiative of the staff, and a realiza-
tion on the part of every member of the Branch that there
is nothing so damaging to the reputation of a body engaged
on secret duties as leakages of information about the
work which is being done.

The following rules are set down for general
guidance :-

1. With the exception of reports on routine matters
and ordinary labour or political affairs, all documents
should as a rule be typed by the officer in charge of
the inquiries.

2. The initials of the person by whom it was typed
should be given at the top of each report.

3. Reports when typed should be handed personally by the
detective responsible for the inquiry to the Officer
in Charge of his Section.

June 21, 1935.

Secrecy in Special Branch.

The Officers in charge of Sections of the Special
Branch should exercise the greatest care in guarding
secrets entrusted to their keeping, and it is incumbent
on all members of the staff to assist their seniors in
the discharge of this duty by being at pains to prevent
any leakage of information about inquiries on which they
are engaged themselves and by reporting without delay
any circumstance pointing to the possibility of the
existence of a leakage in any division of the office to
which they are attached. While laying down the
following rules for general guidance, the D. C. (Sp.Br.)
feels that the safeguarding of the secrets of the work
of the Branch must finally depend upon the loyalty,
carefulness and initiative of the staff, and a realiza-
tion on the part of every member of the Branch that there
is nothing so damaging to the reputation of a body engaged
on secret duties as leakages of information about the
work which is being done.

The following rules are set down for general
guidance :-

1. With the exception of reports on routine matters
and ordinary labour or political affairs, all documents
should as a rule be typed by the officer in charge of
the inquiries.

2. The initials of the person by whom it was typed
should be given at the top of each report.

3. Reports when typed should be handed personally by the
detective responsible for the inquiry to the Officer
in Charge of his Section.

June 21, 1935.

Secrecy in Special Branch.

The Officers in charge of Sections of the Special
Branch should exercise the greatest care in guarding
secrets entrusted to their keeping, and it is incumbent
on all members of the staff to assist their seniors in
the discharge of this duty by being at pains to prevent
any leakage of information about inquiries on which they
are engaged themselves and by reporting without delay
any circumstance pointing to the possibility of the
existence of a leakage in any division of the office to
which they are attached. While laying down the
following rules for general guidance, the D. C. (Sp.Br.)
feels that the safeguarding of the secrets of the work
of the Branch must finally depend upon the loyalty,
carefulness and initiative of the staff, and a realiza-
tion on the part of every member of the Branch that there
is nothing so damaging to the reputation of a body engaged
on secret duties as leakages of information about the
work which is being done.

The following rules are set down for general
guidance :-

1. With the exception of reports on routine matters
and ordinary labour or political affairs, all documents
should as a rule be typed by the officer in charge of
the inquiries.

2. The initials of the person by whom it was typed
should be given at the top of each report.

3. Reports when typed should be handed personally by the
detective responsible for the inquiry to the Officer
in Charge of his Section.

secrets entrusted to their keeping, and it is incumbent
on all members of the staff to assist their seniors in
the discharge of this duty by being at pains to prevent
any leakage of information about inquiries on which they
are engaged themselves and by reporting without delay
any circumstance pointing to the possibility of the
existence of a leakage in any division of the office to
which they are attached. While laying down the
following rules for general guidance, the D. C. (Sp.Br.)
feels that the safeguarding of the secrets of the work
of the Branch must finally depend upon the loyalty,
carefulness and initiative of the staff, and a realiza-
tion on the part of every member of the Branch that there
is nothing so damaging to the reputation of a body engaged
on secret duties as leakages of information about the
work which is being done.

The following rules are set down for general
guidance :-

1. With the exception of reports on routine matters
and ordinary labour or political affairs, all documents
should as a rule be typed by the officer in charge of
the inquiries.

2. The initials of the person by whom it was typed
should be given at the top of each report.

3. Reports when typed should be handed personally by the
detective responsible for the inquiry to the Officer
in Charge of his Section.

上海公共租界工部局警务处特别科。
1935年6月21日。

特别科的保密工作。

特别科各科科长在保管 entrusted 给他们的秘密时，应极其谨慎；全体职员均有责任协助上级履行此项职责，务必防止泄露其自身所从事调查工作的任何信息，并立即报告任何表明其所属部门可能存在泄密情况的事由。在制定以下一般性指导规则时，特别科副总监认为，保护本科工作秘密最终必须依赖于职员的忠诚、谨慎和主动性，以及本科每位成员都认识到：对于从事秘密工作的机构而言，没有什么比泄露正在进行的工作信息更损害其声誉的了。

现制定以下规则以供一般性指导：-

1. 除关于日常事务及普通劳工或政治事件的报告外，所有文件原则上应由负责该调查的警官打字。

2. 每份报告的顶部应注明打字人的姓名首字母。

3. 报告打字完成后，应由负责该调查的探员亲自交给其所在科的科长。

pages.en:
- 2 -

4. On receiving a report the Officer in Charge of the
Section should see that they are stamped "Secret"
and passed without undue delay either personally or
in a locked or sealed container to the Officer in
Charge of the Registry.

5. The Officer in Charge of the Registry will handle all
confidential files passing to and from the D. C. (Sp.Br.)
and will attend personally to the indexing and filing
of these reports in the cabinet provided.

6. The Officer in Charge of the Registry should arrange
as soon as circumstances permit after the receipt of
confidential reports to show them to the P. A. to
D. C. (Sp.Br.) so that the latter will be acquainted
with all work undertaken in the Branch.

7. Copies of reports made by S. 2 should be retained
and kept effectively locked up by the Officer in Charge.
Not more than one spare copy of a report should be
retained by any Section, and special measures should be
taken in every case to ensure that these copies are
only seen by members of the staff who actually require
them in connection with their work.

8. Confidential files will only be obtainable from the
Registry upon production of an application form signed
by an Officer in Charge of a Section. Before handing
out a file of a specially secret nature or otherwise
of extraordinary importance, the Officer in Charge
of the Registry should refer the matter to the P. A.
or the D. C. (Sp.Br.) Applications for files should
be submitted in sealed covers and handed into the
Registry through the clerk at the Inquiry Desk. The
files should be sent to the officers by whom they are
required either personally by a responsible member of
the staff of the Registry or in a sealed cover.
pages.zh:
- 2 -

4. 科长收到报告后，应确保报告盖上“秘密”印章，并无不当延误地亲自或通过上锁或密封的容器，将其转交给档案室科长。

5. 档案室科长将处理所有往来于特别科副总监处的机密卷宗，并亲自负责将这些报告索引并存入指定的柜中。

6. 档案室科长应在收到机密报告后，视情况尽快安排向特别科副总监助理展示这些报告，以便后者了解本科开展的所有工作。

7. 第二股（S. 2）制作的报告副本应由科长保留并有效锁存。任何一股保留的报告备用副本不得超过一份，且在每种情况下均应采取特别措施，确保只有因工作需要而确实需要查看这些副本的职员才能看到。

8. 只有凭某科科长签名的申请表，方可从档案室获取机密卷宗。在分发具有特别秘密性质或其他格外重要的卷宗之前，档案室科长应将此事报请特别科副总监助理或特别科副总监批示。申请卷宗应装入密封信封，并通过问询台办事员递交至档案室。卷宗应由档案室的一名负责任职员亲自送达，或通过密封信封发送给所需军官。

pages.en:
- 3 -

9. Applications for files received during the previous
twenty four hours should be submitted to the D.C.
(Sp.Br.) every morning at 10 a.m.

10. Notes and drafts of reports on confidential matters
should be destroyed by fire. Carbon paper used in
the typing of such reports should be locked up when
not in use. Drafts of reports should be made in
pencil so as to eliminate the possibility of leakages
of information through blotting paper.

11. Detectives' diaries and other papers containing notes
on cases should at all times be kept locked up. In
special cases detectives should be instructed not
to give details in their diaries of addresses visited
or names of persons about whom information is sought.
A blank space could be left and filled up after the
necessity for secrecy elapses.

12. The transmitting of messages of a secret nature by
telephone . should as far as possible be avoided.

13. All chit books and letters brought to headquarters by
messengers and others should in the first instance
be handed to the clerk at the Inquiry Desk who will
take them to the Officer in the Registry appointed to
receive and acknowledge such communications. He will
return the chit books or receipts to the messengers
after they have been duly signed.

14. All persons wishing to see the D. C. (Sp.Br.) or any
person working in Room 614, occupied by the Registry,
should present themselves at the Inquiry Desk and
arrange to see the person they are seeking by filling
up a slip on which they will state their own name,
the name of the person they wish to see and the nature
of their business. If the person sought happens to be
out, the slip should be taken to an appropriate
substitute.
pages.zh:
- 3 -

9. 前二十四小时内收到的卷宗申请，应于每日上午10时提交给特别科副总监。

10. 关于机密事项的笔记和报告草稿应予焚毁。用于打印此类报告的复写纸在不使用时应锁存。报告草稿应用铅笔书写，以消除通过吸墨纸泄露信息的可能性。

11. 探员日记及其他包含案件笔记的文件应随时锁存。在特殊情况下，应指示探员不要在日记中记录所访问的地址或正在查询信息的人员姓名。可留出空白，待保密必要性消失后再行填写。

12. 应尽可能避免通过电话传递秘密性质的信息。

13. 信差及其他人员送至总部的所有便条簿和信件，首先应交给问询台办事员，由其转交给档案室指定负责接收并确认此类通信的官员。该官员在 duly 签署后，将便条簿或收据退还给信差。

14. 所有希望会见特别科副总监或在由档案室占用的614房间工作的任何人员者，应前往问询台，并通过填写一张 slips 来安排会见，slip 上需注明其本人姓名、希望会见者的姓名以及事由性质。如果被寻找的人恰好外出，该 slip 应交给适当的代理人。

pages.en:
- 4 -

15. Nobody is to be allowed to loiter in any Section and
nobody, apart from Officers in Charge of Sections,
should enter the Registry. Members of the public
should on no account be allowed to enter the
Registry unless brought there by the D. C. (Sp.Br.)
or an officer acting for him.

16. All communications with other branches of the Force
should be sent in special locked boxes.

17. Weekly Returns of Reports should not state the
subject to which they refer.

18. When files of an exceptionally confidential nature
or of great urgency have to be dealt with, the
D. C. (Sp. Br.) may depart from these rules and
make special arrangements in regard to the procedure
to be followed.

J.W. Givens
Deputy Commissioner
(Special Branch)
pages.zh:

15. 任何人不得在任何一股内逗留闲逛；除各科科长外，任何人不得进入档案室。公众人士绝不允许进入档案室，除非由特别科副总监或代表其行事的官员带入。

16. 与本局其他部门的所有通信应通过特制的上锁信箱发送。

17. 每周报告汇总表中不应陈述其所涉及的主题。

18. 当需要处理具有格外机密性质或非常紧急的卷宗时，特别科副总监可以偏离这些规则，并就应遵循的程序作出特别安排。

副总监

Municipal Advocate.

"The Objectionable Advertisements"

Acting upon your instruction, I have interviewed Chief Judge Dzien of the Shanghai First Special Area District Court with regard to the above entitled subject. After reading over all the advertisements, he is of the opinion that both the advertisers and the newspaper publishers are liable for disturbing the public peace and order as well as for being prejudicial to good morals. He also suggests that the advertisers and the publishers be again warned by the S. M. Police and that in case the warning is ignored, the advertisers be charged under Articles 21, 25 and 43 of the Revised Press Law and the publishers under Articles 22, 25 and 44 of the same law.

The full text of the Revised Press Law as promulgated on July 8, 1937 and its rough translation are herewith attached.

Approved:
D&B
March 26th 1938

Thomas Tea
Assistant Municipal Advocate.

“令人反感的广告”

遵照您的指示，我就上述标题事宜采访了上海第一特区地方法院首席法官 Dzien（音译）。在审阅所有广告后，他认为广告商和报纸出版商均对扰乱公共治安秩序以及妨害善良风俗负有责任。他还建议由上海公共租界警务处再次警告广告商和出版商，若无视警告，则依据《修正出版法》第21、25和43条起诉广告商，并依据同一法律的第22、25和44条起诉出版商。

THE REVISED PRESS LAW
(Promulgated by the National Govern-
ment on July 8, 1937)

CHAPTER I - GENERAL PROVISIONS

Article 1. The word "publication" referred to in
this Law denotes books, articles, pictures and drawings
printed by mechanical means or by chemical processes
or in block types for sale and distribution.

Article 2. (I) Publications shall be divided into
the following three kinds:-
(a) Newspapers: denoting publications under specific
names continuously published, daily or at
intervals of less than six days.
(b) Magazines: denoting publications under specific
names continuously published, weekly or at
intervals of less than three months. If, however,
the contents of such publications consist chiefly
of current events, they shall be classified as
newspapers.
(c) Books and other publications: denoting publica-
tions not enumerated in above two sub-sections.
(II) The extras or additional or supplementary
sections of newspapers or magazines shall be regarded as
newspapers or magazines.

Article 3. The word "publisher" referred to in this
Law denotes persons who manage and control the publishing
of publications.

Article 4. (I) The word "author" referred to in this
Law denotes persons who write articles or who make drawings
or pictures.
(II) Recorders who take down speeches for
publication or supply the same to others for publication
shall be considered authors. But speakers who give consent
to publication of the speeches shall also assume the
responsibility of an author.
(III) Compilers of articles shall be consi-
dered authors, but the original authors who gave consent
to the compilation shall also assume the responsibility
of an author.
(IV) Translators of articles shall be con-
sidered as authors.
(V) Representatives of schools, companies,
associations, societies or other organizations shall be
considered authors of publications published in the name of
such schools, companies, associations, societies or
organizations.
(VI) Persons who insert advertisements or
notices in newspapers shall be considered authors of such
advertisements or notices. In case such persons are
unknown or are not competent to accept legal responsibility
in civil matters, the publishers of the newspapers shall be
considered as the authors.

第一章 - 总则

第一条 本法所称“出版物”，系指以机械方法、化学过程或活字排版印刷，供出售及发行之书籍、文章、图片及图画。

第二条 （一）出版物分为下列三种：-
(a) 新闻纸：系指有一定名称，每日或间隔六日以内继续发行者。
(b) 杂志：系指有一定名称，每周或间隔三月以内继续发行者。但其内容以时事为主者，以新闻纸论。
(c) 书籍及其他出版物：系指前两款所未列举之出版物。
（二）新闻纸或杂志之号外、增刊或附刊，视为新闻纸或杂志。

第三条 本法所称“发行人”，系指管理并支配出版物发行之人。

第四条 （一）本法所称“著作人”，系指撰述文字或绘制图画之人。
（二）记录演讲供发表或供给他人发表之记录人，视为著作人。但同意发表之演讲人，亦负著作人之责任。
（三）编辑文章之人，视为著作人。但同意编辑之原著作人，亦负著作人之责任。
（四）翻译文章之人，视为著作人。
（五）学校、公司、协会、社团或其他组织以其名义发行出版物者，其代表人视为著作人。
（六）在新闻纸上刊登广告或启事之人，视为该广告或启事之著作人。如该等人不明或无民事法律责任能力时，以该新闻纸之发行人为著作人。

Article 6. The word "printer" referred to in this Law denotes persons who are responsible for the printing of matters.

Article 7. The term "district official organ" referred to in this Law denotes a Hsien Government or a City Government in a province, or a Bureau of Social Affairs of a City Government under the direct control of the Executive Yuan.

Article 8. (I) Publishers shall submit one copy of each publication to each of the following organs:-
(1) The Ministry of Interior.
(2) The Central Propaganda Department.
(3) The District Official Organ.
(4) The National Central Library and
The Library of the Legislative Yuan.
(II) Copies of the revised edition of a publication shall also be sent to these organs.
(III) Copies of publications made by official or Kuomintang organs shall be sent by post to the organs as provided in the two preceding sections.

CHAPTER II - NEWSPAPERS AND MAGAZINES

Article 9. (I) Before the first issue publishers of newspapers or magazines shall apply for registration to the district official organ in whose district the publishing offices are located. The district official organ shall within 15 days after the receipt of the application, refer it to the Provincial Government or the City Government under the direct control of the Executive Yuan. The approval of the Provincial Government or the City Government is necessary before publication can be made.
(II) The Provincial or City Government upon receipt of the above mentioned application shall, except in special cases, hand down a decision within 28 days and if it approves the application, request the Ministry of Interior to issue a Registration Certificate. After issuing the certificate, the Ministry of Interior shall send a copy of the application to the Central Propaganda Department. The following particulars shall be given in the application for registration:-
(a) The name of the newspaper or magazine.
(b) The organization of the newspaper or magazine office.
(c) The amount of capital and the financial conditions of the concern.
(d) The period of publication. In case of newspapers, the number of pages of each issue shall be stated.
(e) The names and addresses of the printing and publishing offices.
(f) The names, ages, biography and residence address of the publishers and editors.

Article 10. (I) When a change is made in any of the particulars registered in accordance with Article 9, an application for amendment shall be made within 7 days after the change, the procedure being same as that adopted when applying for registration.

第二章 - 新闻纸及杂志

第九条 （一）新闻纸或杂志在首次发行前，发行人应向出版事务所所在地之地方主管官署申请登记。地方主管官署应于收到申请后十五日内，转呈省政府或行政院直属市政府。须经省政府或行政院直属市政府核准后，方可发行。
（二）省政府或行政院直属市政府收到上述申请后，除特殊情况外，应于二十八日内作出决定；如核准申请，应请求内政部颁发登记证。内政部颁发证书后，应将申请书副本送交中央宣传部。登记申请书应载明下列事项：-
(a) 新闻纸或杂志之名称。
(b) 新闻纸或杂志社之组织结构。
(c) 资本数额及该机构之财务状况。
(d) 发行周期。如为新闻纸，应注明每期页数。
(e) 印刷所及发行所之名称及地址。
(f) 发行人及编辑人之姓名、年龄、履历及居住地址。

第十条 （一）依第九条登记之事项如有变更，应于变更后七日内申请变更登记，其程序与申请登记时相同。

(a) Those who have received criminal punishment for

第十五条 (一) 报纸或杂志停刊时，发行人应依照申请登记时所采用之程序，申请注销登记。
(二) 报纸之出版较规定日期延误三个月以上，或杂志之出版较规定日期延误六个月以上者，该报纸或杂志视为已停刊。

第十六条 每一份报纸或杂志均须刊载发行人姓名、登记证号码、出版日期，以及出版机构和印刷机构之名称及地址。

第十七条 (一) 凡因报纸或杂志刊登之文章而受牵连之人，或与受牵连人有直接关系之人，申请更正或刊登辩驳书者，除所请求之更正或辩驳文字明显违法，或申请人未具名及提供地址，或于原文章刊登六个月后方提出申请外，日报应于收到申请后三日内刊登，定期出版之报纸或杂志应于下一期刊登。
(二) 更正或辩驳书所占篇幅应与原文章相同。

CHAPTER III - BOOKS AND OTHER PUBLICATIONS

Article 18. The names and addresses of the authors
and publishers, the date of publication, the names and
addresses of the publishing and printing offices shall be
recorded on the last page of a book or publication.

Article 19. Article 8 does not apply to notifications,
regulations, business reports, catalogues, handbills,
advertisements, programmes, statistics, certificates, tickets
and photographs.

Article 20. No handbills or slogans relating to
political matters shall be printed or published without the
approval of the district official organ.

CHAPTER IV - LIMITATION OF ITEMS FOR PUBLICATION

Article 21. The publication of comments or propaganda
reports of the following nature is prohibited:-
(a) Those intended to ruin the Kuomintang or to
violate the Three Principles of the People.
(b) Those intended to subvert the National Government
or are prejudicial to the interests of the
Republic of China.
(c) Those intended to disturb the public peace and
order.

Article 22. The publication of articles prejudicial
to good morals is prohibited.

Article 23. Publications shall not publish the
pleadings of Court cases which have not been heard in open
Court.

Article 24. In case of war or emergency or other
special necessity, the National Government may issue orders
prohibiting or restricting the publication of matters
relating to politics, military affairs, diplomacy or local
peace and order.

Article 25. Advertisements, notices etc. published
in publications are subject to the restrictions stipulated
in the preceding four articles.

CHAPTER V - ADMINISTRATIVE ACTION

Article 26. (I) The publication of a newspaper or
magazine may be suppressed if such newspaper or magazine
fails to apply for registration in accordance with Article 9
or gives incorrect particulars in the registration.
(II) The publication of a newspaper or
magazine that has failed to apply for a change in regis-
tration as required by Article 10 may be ordered to be
suspended until the provisions of that Article have been
fulfilled.

Article 27. The action provided for by the preceding
article shall be taken by the Hsien or City Government after
the approval of the Provincial Government has been obtained
if the publication is published at a place wherein a Hsien
or City Government is located. If the publication is published
at a place wherein a Provincial Government or a City Govern-
ment under the direct control of the Executive Yuan is located,

第三章 - 书籍及其他出版物

第十八条 书籍或出版物之末页，须刊载作者及发行人之姓名和地址、出版日期，以及出版机构和印刷机构之名称及地址。

第十九条 第八条之规定不适用于通告、规章、营业报告、目录、传单、广告、节目单、统计资料、证明书、票券及照片。

第二十条 凡涉及政治事项之传单或标语，未经区主管官署核准，不得印刷或发布。

第四章 - 出版物品之限制

第二十一条 禁止刊登下列性质之评论或宣传报道：
(a) 意图破坏中国国民党或违背三民主义者。
(b) 意图颠覆国民政府或损害中华民国利益者。
(c) 意图扰乱公共安宁与秩序者。

第二十二条 禁止刊登有伤风化之文章。

第二十三条 出版物不得刊登未经公开审理之法庭案件之诉辩状。

第二十四条 遇有战争、紧急事变或其他特殊必要时，国民政府得发布命令，禁止或限制刊登有关政治、军事、外交或地方安宁秩序之事项。

第二十五条 出版物内刊登之广告、通告等，须受前四条规定之限制。

第五章 - 行政处分

第二十六条 (一) 报纸或杂志未依照第九条规定申请登记，或登记时填报不实者，得禁止其出版。
(二) 报纸或杂志未依照第十条规定申请变更登记者，得令其暂停出版，直至符合该条规定为止。

第二十七条 前条规定之处分，如出版物在设有县或市政府之地出版，由县或市政府报经省政府核准后执行。如出版物在设有省政府或行政院直属市政府之地出版，

the action shall be taken by the Provincial Government
or the City Government after the approval of the Ministry
of Interior has been obtained. In case approval for
action has been given by a Provincial Government, the
Provincial Government shall later make a report to the
Ministry of Interior for record.

Article 29. (I) If the Ministry of Interior considers
that a publication contains one of the classes of articles
listed in Article 21, or that the publication violates the
prohibitions or restrictions stipulated in Article 24, the
Ministry may indicate such and suppress the sale or
distribution of that publication. If necessary, the
publication may be seized.
(II) The seized publication may be returned
at the request of the publisher after the offensive articles
have been deleted or the order of suppression has been
lifted.
(III) Should the offense be of a trivial
nature, the district official organ may, with the approval
of the Provincial or City Government to which it belongs,
issue a warning. The Provincial or City Government shall,
in such case, make a report to the Ministry of Interior.

Article 30. When a district official organ discovers
one of the classes of publications mentioned in Section I
of the preceding Article, it may, in case of necessity,
temporarily suppress the sale and distribution or seize
the publication and at the same time report to the Pro-
vincial Government or the City Government under the direct
control of the Executive Yuan; the Provincial or City
Government shall in turn report to the Ministry of Interior
who shall deal with the matter.

Article 31. The action provided in the preceding
Article shall be taken by the Provincial Government at the
request of the Hsien or City Government if the publication
is a newspaper or magazine published at a place wherein a
Hsien or City Government is located; the action shall be
taken by the Ministry of Interior at the request of the
Provincial Government or the City Government under the
direct control of the Executive Yuan if the publication is a
newspaper or magazine published at a place wherein a
Provincial Government or a City Government under the direct
control of the Executive Yuan is located.

Article 32. (I) If a publication published abroad is
found to be liable to actions provided in Section 1 of
Article 28 or Section 1 of Article 34, the Ministry of
Interior may ban its importation.
(II) A publication thus banned shall, if
imported, be seized, at the time of its importation, by
the Provincial Government or the City Government.

Article 33. (I) If a newspaper or magazine has committed
one of the offences described in Section 1 of Article 28,
and if the offence is of a serious nature, the publication
of such a newspaper or magazine may, by order of the
Ministry of Interior, be suppressed permanently or for a
certain period of time.
(II) Newspapers or magazines published in
defiance of a suppression order mentioned in the preceding
section shall be seized by the district official organ.

第二十九条 (一) 内政部如认为出版物含有第二十一条所列各类文章之一，或违反第二十四条所规定之禁令或限制者，得指出该项情事，并禁止该出版物之销售或分发。必要时，得扣押该出版物。
(二) 被扣押之出版物，于删去违禁文章或解除禁令后，得依发行人之请求予以发还。
(三) 如情节轻微，区主管官署得报经所属省或市政府核准，予以警告。省或市政府在此情况下，应报内政部备案。

第三十条 区主管官署如发现前条第一款所述各类出版物之一，必要时得暂时禁止其销售及分发，或扣押该出版物，并同时报告省政府或行政院直属市政府；省政府或市政府应转报内政部，由内政部处理此事。

第三十一条 前条规定之处分，如出版物为在设有县或市政府之地出版之报纸或杂志，由县政府或市政府请求省政府执行；如出版物为在设有省政府或行政院直属市政府之地出版之报纸或杂志，由省政府或行政院直属市政府请求内政部执行。

第三十二条 (一) 国外出版之刊物，如发现其应受第二十八条第一款或第三十四条第一款规定之处分者，内政部得禁止其进口。
(二) 此项被禁刊物如已进口，由省政府或市政府于进口时予以扣押。

第三十三条 (一) 报纸或杂志如有第二十八条第一款所述之违法行为，且情节严重者，内政部得命令永久或定期禁止该报纸或杂志之出版。
(二) 违反前款禁令而出版之报纸或杂志，由区主管官署予以扣押。

Article 33. (I) When books or other publications are seized, the type forms of such books or publications may, if necessary, be also seized.
(II) The stipulation of Section 2 of Article 28 applies to the seized type forms.

Article 34. (I) In addition to being dealt with according to law when the contents of a publication violate the Criminal Code, the publication, when it violates Article 22 of this Law, and when such a violation is of a serious nature, may have its sale and distribution suppressed and if necessary, it may be seized by the Ministry of Interior or by the district official organ with the approval of the Ministry of Interior.
(II) In case the publication is a newspaper or magazine, it may be suppressed for a certain period of time.

Article 35. A publisher who fails to submit his publication in accordance with Article 8, Sections 1 or 2, shall be fined a sum of not more than $30.

Article 36. A person who publishes a newspaper or magazine without applying for registration according to Article 9 or 10 shall be fined a sum of not more than $100.

Article 37. Any one of the persons mentioned in Article 13 or 14 publishing or editing a newspaper or magazine shall be fined a sum of not more than $100.

Article 38. A fine of not more than $20 shall be imposed upon a publisher who violates Section 1 of Article 15.

Article 39. A fine of not more than $100 shall be imposed upon a publisher whose publication does not contain the record required by Article 16 or 18 or if the particulars recorded are incorrect.

Article 40. An editor violating Article 17 shall be fined a sum of not more than $100.

Article 41. When a newspaper, having been subject to administrative action provided in this Chapter by an official organ, appeals to the superior organ of that organ, the superior organ shall hand down a decision within 10 days after the receipt of the appeal.

CHAPTER VI - PENALTIES

Article 42. A fine of not more than $100 shall be imposed upon a publisher or printer who violates Article 20.

Article 43. The publisher, editor, author and printer shall be punished with imprisonment of not more than one year or detention or a fine of not more than $1,000 for violation of Article 21. When heavier punishments are provided in other laws, such laws shall be applied.

Article 44. The editor or author shall be sentenced to a term of detention or a fine of not more than $300 for violation of Article 22 or 23.

第三十三条 (一) 扣押书籍或其他出版物时，必要时亦得扣押该书或出版物之铅版。
(二) 第二十八条第二款之规定，适用于被扣押之铅版。

第三十四条 (一) 出版物内容违反刑法者，除依法处理外，如违反本法第二十二条且情节严重者，得由内政部或经内政部核准之区主管官署禁止其销售及分发，必要时并得予以扣押。
(二) 如该出版物为报纸或杂志，得定期禁止其出版。

第三十五条 发行人未依照第八条第一款或第二款规定送交出版物者，处三十元以下罚款。

第三十六条 未依照第九条或第十条规定申请登记而出版报纸或杂志者，处一百元以下罚款。

第三十七条 第十三条或第十四条所述人员出版或编辑报纸或杂志者，处一百元以下罚款。

第三十八条 发行人违反第十五条第一款者，处二十元以下罚款。

第三十九条 出版物未载有第十六条或第十八条规定之记录，或所载事项不实者，对发行人处一百元以下罚款。

第四十条 编辑违反第十七条者，处一百元以下罚款。

第四十一条 报纸经官署依本章规定给予行政处分后，向该官署之上級官署提起申诉者，上级官署应于收到申诉后十日内作出决定。

第六章 - 罚则

第四十二条 出版人或印刷人违反第二十条者，处一百元以下罚款。

第四十三条 违反第二十一条者，对发行人、编辑、作者及印刷人处一年以下有期徒刑、拘役或一千元以下罚款。其他法律有更重处罚规定者，适用该法律规定。

第四十四条 违反第二十二条或第二十三条者，对编辑或作者处拘役或三百元以下罚款。

Article 45. The publisher, editor, author and printer
shall be punished with imprisonment of not more than
one year or detention or a fine of not more than $1,000
for violation of the prohibitions or restrictions laid
down in Article 24.

Article 46. In the case of newspapers or magazines,
the author of an article is liable to the penalties
provided in Article 43 only when he has signed and expressed
his willingness to assume responsibility for the article.
The same stipulation applies to Article 45.

Article 47. A person who publishes a newspaper or
magazine the publication of which has been ordered to be
stopped in accordance with Article 26, shall be punished
with a fine of not more than $200.

Article 48. A person who obstructs the execution of
an order for the seizure stipulated in Article 29 shall be
punished with a fine of not more than $200.

Article 49. (I) A publisher who contravenes the sup-
pression mentioned, in Article 28, Section 1, shall be
punished with imprisonment of not more than one year or
detention or a fine of not more than $1,000. A person
who knowingly sells or distributes such publications
shall be punished with imprisonment of not more than six
months or detention or a fine of not more than $500.
(II) The above provisions apply to persons
who contravene the ban mentioned in Article 31, Section 1,
or to those who knowingly import, sell or distribute the
publications mentioned therein.

Article 50. A person who obstructs the execution of an
order for seizure stipulated in Section 1 of Article 28,
Section 2 of Article 31, Section 2 of Article 32 and Article
33, shall be punished with imprisonment of not more than
six months or detention or a fine of not more than $500.

Article 51. Publishers who contravene the suppression
mentioned in Section 1 of Article 32 shall be punished with
imprisonment of not more than one year or detention or a
fine of not more than $1,000. Persons who knowingly sell
or distribute such newspapers or magazines shall be punished
with imprisonment of not more than six months or detention
or a fine of not more than $500.

Article 52. The right of prosecution for offences
under this law shall be barred if it is not exercised
within one year. For offences under Articles 43 and 45,
the right of prosecution starts from date of publication.

CHAPTER VII - APPENDIX

Article 53. The regulations governing the enforcement
of this Law shall be drawn up by the Ministry of Interior.

Article 54. This Law shall come into force on the
date of its promulgation.

第四十五条。出版人、编辑、作者及印刷人，如违反第二十四条所规定的禁令或限制，应处以一年以下有期徒刑、拘役或一千元以下罚金。

第四十六条。就报纸或杂志而言，文章作者仅在签名并表示愿意对该文章承担责任的情况下，方须承担第四十三条规定的处罚。同一规定亦适用于第四十五条。

第四十七条。出版依第二十六条命令停止出版的报纸或杂志者，应处以二百元以下罚金。

第四十八条。阻碍执行第二十九条规定的扣押命令者，应处以二百元以下罚金。

第四十九条。（一）出版人违反第二十八条第一款所述之查禁规定者，应处以一年以下有期徒刑、拘役或一千元以下罚金。明知而销售或分发此类出版物者，应处以六个月以下有期徒刑、拘役或五百元以下罚金。（二）上述规定适用于违反第三十一条第一款所述之禁令者，或明知而进口、销售或分发该条所述出版物者。

第五十条。阻碍执行第二十八条第一款、第三十一条第二款、第三十二条第二款及第三十三条规定的扣押命令者，应处以六个月以下有期徒刑、拘役或五百元以下罚金。

第五十一条。出版人违反第三十二条第一款所述之查禁规定者，应处以一年以下有期徒刑、拘役或一千元以下罚金。明知而销售或分发此类报纸或杂志者，应处以六个月以下有期徒刑、拘役或五百元以下罚金。

第五十二条。本法规定之犯罪，其追诉权如在一年内不行使，即告消灭。第四十三条及第四十五条规定之犯罪，其追诉权自出版之日起算。

第七章 - 附则

第五十三条。本法施行细则由内政部制定。

第五十四条。本法自公布之日起施行。
